# Orders

Customers see an order as **pending** right after checkout. Once the warehouse system confirms the
items, the order moves to **reserved**, and to **shipped** once a tracking number exists. Support
can cancel a pending or reserved order from the admin panel; cancelling releases the stock.

## Order statuses in exports
The CSV export uses the same status names. Integration partners should treat unknown statuses as
pending.

Author: Priya Raman <priya@example.com>
Date:   Fri Sep 19 16:02:11 2026 +0200

    Move stock reservation to event listener (#482)

    createOrder() no longer waits on the stock service; reservation happens in StockListener
    when it receives order.created. Keeps checkout fast when the stock DB is slow.

 src/stock/StockListener.ts | 12 ++++++++++++

     await this.orders.insert(order)
-    await this.stock.decrement(order.sku, order.quantity)
-    await this.orders.update(order.id, { stockStatus: 'reserved' })
-    order.stockStatus = 'reserved'
+    this.events.emit('order.created', { orderId: order.id, sku: order.sku, quantity: order.quantity })
     return order

content.text: Hypothesis: since #482, stock is reserved asynchronously by StockListener after createOrder() returns, so the test's assertion races the listener. It only loses when the listener's two DB writes are slower than the test's findById, which is more likely on a loaded CI runner.
